subject: MAP: performance acceptance checklist, TTFT & concurrency gaps, and close runway
messages:

To: Ethan Blake <ethan.blake@astoriahealth.com>, Priya Sen <priya.sen@astoriahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP kickoff — perf acceptance checklist & quick asks

Hi Ethan / Priya —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation I'd like to lock the MAP items that will unblock your procurement and the final close. High level ask: we need a short acceptance plan (1–2 runs) that validates latency/throughput/TTFT at your target concurrency, plus a brief methodology note so we can align on tooling.

Proposed quick MAP items (attached as MAP v2):
- Acceptance criteria doc with target SLOs: p95 latency <= 220ms, TTFT <= 450ms at 8 concurrent users; sustainable throughput 180 reqs/min (burst 240)
- Two scheduled benchmark runs from your environment (same dataset): one at baseline, one with our suggested batching/cache settings
- Shared repro steps & logs for any divergence (we'll provide an internal triage playbook)
- Contract runway: target signature by 2026-04-02 if acceptance passes

Can you confirm: 1) the targets above match what you expect, 2) who will run the tests on your side (or would you like Redwood to execute)? If you'd like us to run, we can supply a small canary config and runbook.

Attachments: redwood_map_v2.xlsx (MAP with timeline & owners)

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — perf acceptance checklist & quick asks

Vanessa —

Thanks, the MAP looks reasonable. Quick answers:
- Targets: p95 latency target is OK; TTFT target we may need to relax to 500ms at 8 concurrent sessions for the initial run (our current infra has heavier request pre-processing).
- We'll run the tests from our staging cluster (staging-nyc). Primary contact: Ethan (me) and Priya will coordinate procurement timelines.

We've attached the baseline run we just did (perf_results_20260322.csv). To call out one discrepancy: our TTFT numbers are ~30% higher than your public benchmarks for similar model/config. The test harness we used is an internal runner built on top of Locust plus some custom request framing; I included ddT logs (ddt_tooling_diff.log) showing header differences.

We'll be able to execute two runs this week if Redwood provides the canary config and exact request framing. Procurement note: our SOW approval depends on a one-week acceptance window after successful runs.

—Ethan
Director of AI Integrations | Astoria Health
ethan.blake@astoriahealth.com

Attachments: perf_results_20260322.csv, ddt_tooling_diff.log

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Blake <ethan.blake@astoriahealth.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 12:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — perf acceptance checklist & quick asks

Ethan — thanks for the results and logs. Quick read of the ddT output suggests two likely causes for the TTFT delta: (1) the request framing includes an extra pre-tokenization step that we're not modeling (adds ~40–60ms per request), and (2) your Locust runner doesn't use continuous batching which affects burst TTFT under concurrency.

I propose the following immediate steps for methodology alignment and triage:
1) Redwood will provide a canary config (json) that mirrors the framing we use in hosted runs — this includes exact headers, tokenization flag, and batching window.
2) We'll supply a minimal repro harness (script + curl examples) so you can run with our exact framing.
3) If delta persists, we'll run a joint remote session where Redwood runs the same workload inside your staging-nyc region to rule out network/infra variance.

Can we get the staging hostnames and a short window this Wed or Thu for a 60–90m joint run? That will help us close the gap quickly and keep the MAP on track for the 2026-04-02 signature target.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Lead Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Hi team —

Thanks for the suggested plan. Procurement/legal context to share: our security team wants the acceptance runs to be reproducible (same binaries + toolchain), and our legal counsel (Morgan) needs a clear MAP timeline to align SOW milestones with signature dates. We can commit to the joint run on Thu 2026-03-25 14:00–15:30 PT.

A couple of asks from our side before the joint session:
- Can Redwood provide the exact canary config and the repro script by EOD Wed (23 Mar)?
- We need a short note on expected variability (network vs. tooling) so our operations team can interpret results quickly.
- Legal asks whether passing acceptance will trigger a 30-day invoice term in the SOW or immediate invoicing upon signature. Morgan, can you confirm?

If the joint run shows the TTFT gap persists and is due to tooling framing, we will accept a remediation plan (timelines + owners) and proceed with signature if that plan is agreeable.

Thanks — Priya
